chunks: And in the narration of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him."
"Meaning: whoever dies, then there is no sin upon him.
"Then there is no sin upon him, for the one who avoids the major sins."

key_terms.تَأَخَّرَ: was delayed; interpreted here as having one's term deferred
key_terms.تَعَجَّلَ: hastened; interpreted here as dying sooner

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explain the verse "So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him"?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir of the verse by interpreting "whoever hastens" as one who dies, and "whoever delays" as one whose appointed term is extended. The closing condition is explained as freedom from sin for the one who has taqwa regarding the major sins, linking the verse to moral accountability.
